Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
6 October 2026 .
Brent $ 98.37 -3.26 % · Transits 4 (2026-10-04) · AI-assisted
01 Iran asserts the strait is closed; Hellenic Shipping News reports Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company moved 2 million barrels of crude through it using a very large crude carrier.

02 Brent stood at $98.37, down 3.26% over 24 hours, as of 14:54 UTC; IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains the central pressure point of the crisis. Oman Observer reports fresh tanker attacks at the strait, and TradeWinds News reports a Maran Gas LNG carrier was struck near it as Iranian attacks mount. The Maran Gas incident is distinct from the October 4 strike on the product tanker Lipsi, which was hit in the engine room and left drifting; Montel News, corroborated by TradeWinds News and gCaptain, reports a projectile struck a third LNG tanker crossing the strait. Ghalibaf and UKMTO context aside, the physical-transit picture is contested: Iran asserts the strait is closed, while Hellenic Shipping News reports Iraq's state-owned Oil Tanker Company moved 2 million barrels of crude through it using a very large crude carrier, its first such operation in decades. IMF PortWatch recorded 4 transits on 2026-10-04, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. Brent stood at $98.37, down 3.26% over 24 hours, as of 14:54 UTC. The feed indexed 66 events in the last 24 hours. As of 14:50 UTC, 201 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, easing over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
